result.title: Asynchronous On-Policy Self-Distillation
result.summary: Unlike on-policy distillation (OPD), which depends on a separate teacher model, on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) leverages a single language model acting simultaneously as the student and the teacher, with the teacher conditioned on privileged information. Despite this architectural simplicity, synchronous rollout generation dominates overall training time, creating a severe systems bottleneck when scaling OPSD. To address this, we introduce Asynchronous On-Policy Self-Distillation (AsyncOPSD), a framework that decouples rollout generation from learner updates to improve training throughput. Since the teacher and student share parameters, AsyncOPSD eliminates the multi-model coordination overhead inherent to OPD architectures in asynchronous training. As the student policy evolves, buffered trajectories generated by older policies become stale, potentially degrading performance. To mitigate this, we introduce a distillation objective based on staleness-aware policy control and token-level entropy weighting. Across three model sizes and mathematical reasoning benchmarks, AsyncOPSD improves the training throughput by $1.96$--$2.25\times$ over synchronous OPSD while increasing average benchmark accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 提出异步 on-policy 自蒸馏（AsyncOPSD），将 rollout 生成与学习者更新解耦以提升训练吞吐，并用陈旧度感知的策略控制与 token 级熵加权缓解缓冲轨迹过期导致的性能下降，在数学推理基准上同时提升吞吐与准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其处理「过时缓冲轨迹」的陈旧度加权与 token 级熵加权，可供核查 LVR 中复用缓存 latent 状态或旧策略轨迹时的训练稳定性与贡献分配问题，属方法线索而非直接研究主线。
